sn45.1:1.1: Detailed explanations for the factors are given in the “Analysis” discourse at [sn45.8]().
sn45.1:2.1: Ignorance begins the sequence of dependent origination, which is said to be the “wrong practice” ([sn12.3]()). | _Pubbaṅgama_ is literally “forerunner”, but rather than indicating something that happens to come in front of something else, the sense is the leader as in the first of a group (see [mn3:6.4]() and especially [an5.180:3.6]()). Thus ignorance, itself an unskillful quality, leads the way for other unskillful qualities to arise.
sn45.1:2.2: Ignorance is the lack of understanding of how the world is, namely the four noble truths. Wrong view crystallizes ignorance in a specific and persistent set of beliefs and ideas.
sn45.1:2.3: This discourse stresses the linear dependence of each factor on the previous. Of course, causality is not so clear cut, and other contexts show the factors working together in various ways (eg. [mn117]()).
sn45.1:3.1: This knowledge originates in learning the Dhamma, reflecting on it, and internalizing the belief.
